note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Actual living source-identified tuft photo (panel 1), flowering panicle (panel 2), leaf with flowering culm (panel 3), and preserved BRIT root+panicle voucher (panel 5). Look for perennial rooted bunch, open drooping flowering head and attached spikelets. The living in-ground photograph hides the actual fibrous root crown; do not certify exposed roots, and do not treat the historical specimen as fresh Hays material.
tiles.status: REAL LIVING TUFT AND FLOWERING ARCHITECTURE NOW PHOTOGRAPHED; EXPOSED ROOT CROWN STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · COUNT ONE SPIKELET
tiles.details: The new true species photograph (panel 4) shows a mature entire multi-flowered spikelet held against a fingertip; panel 3 shows spikelets attached to a flowering culm. Published 6–9 mm length and 2–4 florets remain taxon-level literature, NOT measurements or a dissected glume count established by photos.
tiles.status: SOURCE PHOTOGRAPHS SHOW MATURE WHOLE SPIKELET; CALIBRATED FLORET COUNT PENDING

tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE THE GLUMES
tiles.details: With the same mature spikelet, isolate the 4–7 mm lower glume (1 vein) and 5.5–7 mm upper glume (3 veins); both lack awns. Photograph their intact bases, veins and 1-mm scale. Historical plate supports anatomical orientation only; do not place vein arrows on unreadable pixels.
tiles.status: REPRODUCTIVE PHOTO HELPFUL; TRUE SEPARATED LOWER/UPPER GLUMES STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · AWNLESS LEMMA
tiles.details: Fertile lemma 5–7 mm, obscurely 5-veined, with an acute or acuminate apex, AWNLESS or merely minutely mucronate. A tiny terminal point is not the long projecting awn seen on sixweeks fescue. The 2-veined palea lies within the floret. No present photograph measures these structures.
tiles.short: 5–7 mm, five veins; tiny point possible
tiles.status: WHOLE SPIKELET PHOTO HELPFUL; LEMMA NERVES AND MUCRO NOT MEASURED

tiles.heading: 05 · OPEN THE COLLAR
tiles.details: Expose the inner blade–sheath junction of the same identified plant. The true ligule is a short eciliate (hairless-edged) membrane 0.5–1 mm; leaf blades are generally flat or folded, 2–5 mm wide. Do not infer the ligule from loose spikelets or a sheath edge.

tiles.heading: 06 · SPLIT THE FESCUES
tiles.details: Sixweeks fescue (F. octoflora = Vulpia octoflora) has an annual fibrous base, narrow often crowded panicle, 5–17 florets and an awn on its lemma. Texas fescue has a persistent crown, loose drooping head, 2–4 florets and no long awn. Other woodland fescues can overlap: hold species confirmation without source-vouchered crown and dissected spikelet. Preserve the unresolved Hays occurrence.
tiles.short: Texas perennial and awnless; sixweeks annual and awned

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: TEXAS FESCUE — FIRST check a rooted, persistent PERENNIAL tuft in wooded habitat, with a loose 8–30 cm panicle whose flexible branches droop and carry separate 6–9 mm spikelets (usually 2–4 fertile florets). Then use a hand lens: true hairless-edged MEMBRANOUS ligule 0.5–1 mm; lower glume 4–7 mm and 1-veined, upper 5.5–7 mm and 3-veined; fertile lemma 5–7 mm, 5-veined, AWNLESS or only minutely pointed. Do not confuse the historical F. johnsonii drawing with a modern verified living photo. Current archived photograph is loose fragments and does not independently prove this identification. Compare tiny annual awned F. octoflora, and check other woodland fescues by glume/lemma and rooted crown.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Expose the inner blade–sheath junction of the same identified plant. The true ligule is a short eciliate (hairless-edged) membrane 0.5–1 mm; leaf blades are generally flat or folded, 2–5 mm wide. Do not infer the ligule from loose spikelets or a sheath edge.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: The new true species photograph (panel 4) shows a mature entire multi-flowered spikelet held against a fingertip; panel 3 shows spikelets attached to a flowering culm. Published 6–9 mm length and 2–4 florets remain taxon-level literature, NOT measurements or a dissected glume count established by photos.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: F. octoflora / Vulpia octoflora is a small short-lived annual with very thin leaves and narrow awned upright panicle. F. versuta is a perennial and may show a more branching panicle and an enduring crown; verify this in a fresh whole-plant image because current loose-bract photo cannot separate them reliably. Also compare Festuca subverticillata/nutans concepts with a regional taxonomic key.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.
